caption:
There is a difference between speed and velocity … And it is costing you everything.

Speed is how fast you are moving.
Velocity is how fast you are moving… in the right direction.

You can be incredibly fast… incredibly busy… incredibly productive… and still be going nowhere. Or worse… going the wrong way faster than anyone else in the room.

I see this all the time.

Someone launches a business. It takes off. It feels incredible. And then it falls off. Not because they were not working hard. Because they were running at full speed in a direction that was never going to get them where they needed to go.

In physics… you can run a full lap around a track at top speed and cover a lot of distance… but your velocity is zero. You ended up right where you started. ￼

Business works exactly the same way.

So here is the litmus test I use with every client. Before you take any action… ask yourself one question.

Is this moving me meaningfully toward one of my three goals… finance… growth… or operations.

If the answer is yes… move fast. Go hard. Execute with everything you have.

If the answer is no… it does not matter how fast you are moving.

You are just burning energy going in the wrong direction.

Speed gets you moving.
Velocity gets you there.

Know the difference.

#Business #Growth

caption:
82% of small businesses that fail... 

Fail because of cash flow.

Not because the idea was bad. Not because you weren’t working hard enough. The money ran out before the business had a chance to root down. 

Only half of businesses make it past year five.
The other half didn’t lose to a better competitor. They lost to a forecasting, communication of value, cash reserves they never built.

So … What actually keeps a business alive long enough to succeed...

Forecast weekly. Not monthly. A month is usually too slow to catch a problem before it becomes a crisis. Weekly gives you time to react.

Keep reserves. Stay low leverage. Cash in the bank buys you options. Debt buys you pressure. Make sure this lives in ALL partners personal lives as well. Reserves personally allow the company to survive in tough times. 

Sell better. Not just more. A stronger offer and a clearer close fixes more cash problems than another marketing dollar. 

Invoice faster. Every day you wait to bill is a day someone else is using your money.

Communicate value. Clearly. Often. Customers don’t leave because the product was bad. It’s because they forgot why they were paying for it.

None of this is complicated. It’s just not done consistently.

The businesses that make it past five years aren’t the ones with the best idea. They’re the ones who respected their cash flow like it was the business. Because that’s what it is!

caption:
The line between where you are and where you want to go is razor thin. I’m NOT talking about the end result… I’m talking about the processes you have in your life to get you to where you want to go. They live closer than you think. 

Eating better to cut those last lb’s. 
Sleeping better to get up and be more productive. 
Less time scrolling instead of being present with your family. 
Producing instead of consuming. 
Spending 30mins a week building a process that makes NEXT week easier for you. 

These things are closer than you think. WAY closer. But it comes with an anchor holding you where you are. And the anchor isn’t bad, it’s just what you’ve built. It’s who you are. Your life around you is the foundation. So making even the smallest change, feels hard because there is a rope pulling you back from what you’ve known to be normal. 

And it’s easy to say “I’ll start tomorrow” but as long as those anchors are there, they will continue to hold on tight. 

So cutting those anchors is the hack. And I don’t mean cutting them completely (I.e friends and family. Don’t do that). I mean changing the way YOU see THEM. 
And also changing:
Not buying the groceries 
Putting an alarm in another room so you are forced to wake up early 
Putting apps on your phone to limit the scrolling
Putting up major boundaries in your life to attack processes that make next week easier in your business. 

These habits are all there, right there, on the other side of that razor thin line.

And I am not talking about a bad month here or there.

I am talking about never knowing what is coming in. Feast one month… famine the next. No pattern. No predictability. Just hope.

Here are the 5 most common reasons your revenue is inconsistent… and none of them are the economy. Yes it sucks, but it’s not the reason!

Most of your revenue is walking out the door after the first conversation. You quote it… they go quiet… you move on. 80% of sales happen after the fifth follow up. Most people quit after one. The money is in the follow up and you are not doing it consistently.

2. You are the entire sales process.
If revenue depends entirely on your energy… your mood… your availability… your revenue will look exactly like your schedule. Inconsistent. Build a process that runs without your personal involvement in every step.

3. You have no recurring revenue.
Every month you start at zero and hunt for new money. That is exhausting and unpredictable by design. One retainer client… one monthly package… one subscription changes everything. Build something that pays you before the month starts.

4. You are talking to everyone and closing no one.
Your message is too broad. You are trying to speak to everyone which means you are resonating with no one. When the right person does not feel specifically spoken to… they do not buy. Niche the message. Watch the consistency follow.

5. You have no accountability to your own pipeline.
You know what needs to be done. You are just not doing it consistently. Calls not being made. Content not going out. Follow ups falling through. No one is holding you to the number every single week. That is the gap.

Revenue consistency is not a market problem.

How many times have I said no to something. A trip. A weird opportunity. The success I’m after. Something that scared me a little but probably would’ve been good for me.

And how many times has saying no enough times just... quietly closed that door without me even noticing.

You don’t decide to stop wanting things. You just get told no enough times that you just stop asking.

Same with you probably. Think about what you stopped bringing up. To your partner, your boss, yourself. Probably not because you don’t want it anymore. Probably because you trained yourself to expect the no before you even ask. So you don’t even try. 

We have to be very careful with what we continually say no to or avoid asking because of the anticipated rejection. Especially the things that bring us peace, happiness, the life want or deserve. And just because we heard “no” time and time again … doesn’t mean the no is coming next.

caption:
Some people were built to have the conversations nobody else wants to have.

I am one of them.

And for a long time… I did not fully understand the cost of that.
There is a concept in psychology called conflict avoidance. A large-scale study of over 1,400 adults found that higher levels of conflict avoidance were directly linked to greater psychological distress. Research shows it triggers a genuine stress response in the brain… an amygdala hijack… that causes people to flee from uncomfortable situations even when engaging would produce a far better outcome.

Most people are literally wired to run.

Inside my organization I had partners who ran. Who hid. Who found every possible way to avoid the moment of discomfort a direct conversation requires. So I became the one who had them. Every time. Without hesitation.

And here is where it gets complicated.

When you are consistently the one who speaks the truth… who walks into the room and says what needs to be said… who addresses what nobody else will…
People start to define you by it.
Not by the courage it required. Not by the outcomes it created. Not by the relationships it protected.
By the label.

Difficult. Aggressive. Hard to work with.

That label is not only wrong… it is dangerous.
Because there is a massive difference between who you are and who you have to be inside a given situation.

I did not have those conversations because I enjoy conflict.
I had them because somebody had to.
And the people who should have… were not willing to.

Harvard Business Review found that executives who address conflict rather than avoid it report greater long-term success. Teams that openly discuss difficult issues significantly outperform those that avoid it.

Being willing to say the hard thing is not a character flaw.
It is one of the rarest skills a human being can develop.

Do not let someone else’s avoidance become your reputation.
The world does not need more people who are comfortable.
It needs more people who are willing.

The highs and lows were still happening. They never fully go away. But every single one of them… every high and every low… was sitting higher than the last one.
The whole trajectory was moving up.

The lows got shorter. The highs got higher. And the gap between them got tighter.

Not because the business got easier.
Because they got stronger.
The question is never whether the wave is coming.
It always is.

The question is which wave you decide to quit on.
Because the people who built something real…
They just refused to quit on any of them.

Ever notice this pattern…
The person who actually builds the thing… grows the revenue… brings the clients… put these pieces together … is almost never the one who ends up protected when the relationship goes sideways.
And it goes sideways more than people want to admit.
You think you are on the same side of the table.
You are not always.
So if you are the engine inside of a company… the one doing the real work… the one whose fingerprints are all over the growth… Here are the three things you need to have locked in before it is too late. 

#1: A proper shareholder agreement with REAL exit clauses.
Not a standard boilerplate document someone printed off the internet. A real USA that defines what you are owed for what you contributed… how you exit… and what protects you if the relationship ends on someone else’s terms. Without this… you are at the mercy of whoever holds the most shares.

#2: Document your contribution in real time!!
Every client you brought in. Every system you built. Every process you created. Every revenue milestone you drove. It needs to be on paper… with your name tied to it… before you need it. Because once things go sideways… people forget what you did. Or they choose to forget. And without documentation… it might be harder to have a leg to stand on.

#3: Three. Never give up ownership for future perceived value.
This is the one that gets the most people.
Someone comes to you with a vision. They are excited. They paint a picture of where this is going… what it is going to be worth… what your piece of it will look like when it all comes together.
And you believe them.
So you give up a piece of what you built… a piece of what you own… based on a promise of what they say is coming.
That is not a deal. That is a bet.
And most of the time… you lose.
Here is the rule. Ownership is only given in exchange for value that has already been delivered… not value that is promised down the road.

Do not be blindsided … these tiny little details matter.

But there is something very wrong happening when a generation of people have been sold the idea that the monthly payment is the price.

It is not.

The price is what you pay in total.
A $3,000 item at 10 percent interest over 12 months costs you $163 extra. At 36.99 percent over 24 months… that same purchase costs you over $1,000 in interest alone.

The dangerous part is what happens when this becomes the default setting for every buying decision you make.
When you stop asking “can I afford this” and start asking “can I afford the monthly payment”…
You have stopped building wealth and started renting a lifestyle.

The payment is not the price.
The total is the price.
Save this before the next time you see a checkout screen offering you four easy payments.

Harvard tracked over 700 high achievers for 86 years.
They wanted to know what actually predicted success in life.

Not grades. Not the school you went to. Not the sports you played or the extracurriculars on your resume.

The single biggest predictor of professional success and happiness in adulthood?

Whether or not you did chores as a kid. Yes you read that right. 

A separate 20-year University of Minnesota study backed it up with something even more specific.

The best predictor of success in your mid-20s was whether you started doing chores at age 3 or 4!!! Not 15. Not when you were old enough to understand why. Three or four years old.

And here is why that matters way beyond a clean house.
Chores teach a child something no classroom ever will.
They teach them that the world does not automatically do things for you.
That effort produces outcomes.
That you are part of something bigger than yourself and your contribution actually matters.
That when something needs to be done … you do not wait for someone else to do it first.

That is not a cleaning lesson.
That is the foundation of every successful adult I have ever met.

And yet right now only 28 percent of parents regularly assign chores to their kids.
Even though 82 percent of those same parents grew up doing them.

We know this works. The data is not new. We just stopped doing it.

Because it is easier to do it yourself. Because they complain. Because they have homework. Because you feel bad.
I get it. The struggle can be real. 

But you are not doing them a favour by removing the struggle.
You are removing the lesson.

Give your kids chores. Start early. Be consistent. Do not negotiate.
The dishes can wait. Their future cannot.

caption:
Intergenerational issues don’t come from nowhere. They’re built over time.

For generations in Canada, many white families were given access to things that Indigenous and Black communities were denied (land ownership, stable housing, credit, education, and the ability to build wealth and pass it down). I studied this as a Human Justice major, and I also come at it from a place of privilege …. as a white business owner. That perspective helps me understand why some people land where they do on this topic, especially when education or mindset is limited.

My goal isn’t to shame or point fingers. It’s to add context, share perspective, and help people see the full picture …because that’s how we actually move forward.

So again … that access mattered.

Wealth compounds.
Stability compounds.
Opportunity compounds.
And so do disadvantages.

When communities are blocked from ownership, capital, and safety for decades, the effects don’t reset just because laws change. They carry forward (financially, socially, and emotionally).

That’s what people mean by intergenerational impact.

This is also why these topics are being discussed in schools.
Not to make kids feel guilty.
Not to assign blame.

But to build awareness.

White privilege doesn’t mean every white person had an easy life.
It means the system made it easier for some families to build roots … while making it much harder for others to do the same.

And awareness isn’t something to be ashamed of.
It’s something to understand.

As parents, this is an opportunity … not a threat.
Instead of questioning why it’s being taught, we can use it as a starting point for deeper conversations at home about history, context, and empathy.

Because if we don’t talk about the past,
how do we expect the next generation to learn from it?

Understanding history isn’t about living in it.
It’s about moving forward with clarity.

And that starts with honest conversations … in classrooms AND at the kitchen table.

caption:
The Courage to Be Disliked” is one of those books that hits harder the further you are in your life or career. 

Because its main message is brutally simple:
Most of what’s holding you back isn’t the world…It’s the story you tell yourself about the world.

The book’s core ideas flip the usual mindset completely:
1. Your past does NOT determine your future.
Stop hiding behind “this is just how I am.”
That’s a choice … not a destiny.
2. You suffer when you try to live for other people’s approval.
If your confidence is built on validation, it’s fragile.
If it’s built on purpose, it’s unshakeable.

3. Separate your tasks from everyone else’s.
Your job… is to do the work.
Not your job: control how people react to it.
The moment you stop living for reactions, you get your power back.

4. True freedom is the courage to be disliked.
This isn’t reckless. It’ s not rude. You are just willing to stand firmly in who you are and what you’re building — even if some people don’t like it.

Why this matters for your business, career, and leadership:
Because everything you want (bigger income, better clients, stronger relationships, more confidence) … sits on the other side of dropping the need to be liked by everyone.

You can’t grow and stay small at the same time.
You can’t lead and seek approval at the same time.
You can’t build something meaningful while tiptoeing around opinions.

The book isn’t about being disliked.
It’s about being free enough to succeed.

If your sales are inconsistent, debt tightens the noose.
If your operations aren’t dialed in, debt exposes every weakness.

They use it after they’ve already built something stable.

Build cash flow first.
Build demand first.

Debt isn’t a growth strategy.
